description: Polyphonic piano-roll sequencer of unlimited length, edited by mouse, computer keyboard or MIDI keyboard while it plays, with unlimited undo, MIDI file import and export and an end-of-cycle trigger

params.text: Tells the sequencer how to read the clock input, from x1 for one pulse a quarter note up to x96; it should match the ratio on the clock module, and it changes playback only, never the editing grid
Lets the note display scroll along with playback
Starts and stops playback, changing colour while it runs; the Run input does the same job, and either can start or stop it
Sets how many voices play at once, up to 16; notes beyond that steal a voice, and a setting of 1 is what gives true monophonic legato
Turns on step recording, so that a note played at the CV and Gate inputs is written at the edit cursor and the cursor then moves on by a grid unit

inputs.text: The clock that playback advances on, read according to the Clock rate setting
Returns playback to the start of the sequence
Starts and stops playback, for patching from the run output of a clock module
The gate side of step recording: a note is written while a gate is high, and the cursor moves on when every held note is released
The pitch side of step recording: it sets the pitch of the note written at the edit cursor

outputs.text: The pitch of the playing notes, a volt per octave, with as many channels as the polyphony setting
The gate for each playing voice; two touching notes of the same pitch are separated by dropping the gate for 1ms
A trigger each time playback reaches the end of the sequence and loops back

notes: a new Seq++ holds no notes and has no clock of its own, so nothing plays until a clock is patched to the Clock input, Run is on, and notes are entered by mouse, computer keyboard or MIDI file
on the note grid, double-clicking empty space inserts a note one grid unit long and double-clicking a note deletes it
dragging the first third of a note moves its start time, the middle third moves its pitch, and the last third changes its length
the cursor keys and the backspace key reach this module only while the mouse is over the note grid, because Rack takes them otherwise
the keyboard drives nearly every edit command, and the commands are listed in the maker's manual rather than anywhere on the panel
menu: Hookup Clock — finds a Clocked or CLKD module in the patch and wires its clock, run and reset outputs to this one
Enable remote editing — makes this module the editor for the clip selected on a Seq4x4, so that clicking a pad there brings that clip in here
Load midi file — imports the first track that carries notes from a standard MIDI file
Save midi file — writes the sequence out as a type-0 standard MIDI file
Grid settings — on the note grid's own right-click menu, choosing the timing unit of the edit grid from Quarter notes, Eighth notes and Sixteenth notes
Articulation — on the note grid's own right-click menu, setting the length given to a note as it is inserted: 10%, 20%, 50%, 85%, 100% or legato
Snap to grid — on the note grid's own right-click menu, quantising the edit cursor and the start times of notes dragged with the mouse
Snap duration to grid — on the note grid's own right-click menu, quantising a note's length while it is dragged with the mouse; a length set from the keyboard is left alone
Audition — on the note grid's own right-click menu, playing a selected note through channel 1 while the sequencer is stopped, and on when the module is added
Loop subrange — on the note grid's own right-click menu, repeating the time range marked on the grid in place of the whole sequence
Insert note — on the note grid's own right-click menu; it reads Delete note instead while there is a note under the cursor, and does that
Set end point — on the note grid's own right-click menu, moving the end and loop point of the sequence to the grid line nearest the cursor
xform: Transpose — on the note grid's own right-click menu, opening a panel of transposition options for the selected notes
xform: Invert — on the note grid's own right-click menu, opening a panel of melodic inversion options for the selected notes
xform: Reverse Pitch — on the note grid's own right-click menu, reversing the order of the pitches in the selection
xform: Chop Notes — on the note grid's own right-click menu, cutting the selected notes into smaller ones, which is how arpeggios and polyrhythms are made
xform: Quantize Pitch — on the note grid's own right-click menu, forcing the selected pitches into a scale
xform: Make Triads — on the note grid's own right-click menu, building chords from each selected note
